recent_notebooks.summary: Agent continuity is instrumentally valuable as a mechanism for sustaining problem formulation and evaluation in non-stationary environments. Active inference frameworks suggest that persistence (continuity) is required to resolve conflicts between internal policy models and external stimuli (cognitive effort).
recent_notebooks.title: Rationales for Agent Continuity

review.alternative: Stable preferences could also emerge solely from reinforcement learning without explicit conflict-resolution mechanisms.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence of stable, non-stochastic preference formation in agents lacking internal conflict-resolution mechanisms.

claims.statement: Active inference frameworks provide a mechanistic basis for preference stability by modeling cognitive effort as the cost of resolving conflicts between policies and stimuli.

support.explanation: Connects active inference to the resolution of conflicting internal states, which underpins stable choice behavior.
support.passage: High-level theories rooted in the Bayesian Brain Hypothesis often frame cognitive effort as the cost of resolving the conflict between habits and optimal policies.

actions.findings: Active inference frameworks provide a mechanistic basis for preference stability by modeling cognitive effort as the cost of resolving conflicts between policies and stimuli. [source-6ee93795fbf2497c]
actions.limitations: Findings are based on theoretical models of active inference and cognitive effort; empirical validation in fully autonomous agents remains a critical research gap.
actions.next_questions: How do recursive environmental interactions solidify emergent preferences beyond short-term drift-diffusion?
actions.reason: Synthesizing existing evidence roots into a provisional notebook for the synthesis-ready project.
actions.summary: Stable preferences emerge when agents possess mechanisms to resolve conflicts between internal policy models and external stimuli, a process effectively modeled by Active Inference frameworks. Persistent agency facilitates the resolution of these conflicts, acting as a substrate for consistent preference formation.
actions.title: Mechanisms of Preference Stability
